editorial.headline: Private Hospitality Training: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers privately run job training that builds hospitality skills, open across every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally.
editorial.body:
Private hospitality job training belongs here when the activity is organised by a private provider and is intended to add practical skills or expertise in hospitality. The focus is training work: building capability in a field defined by hotels and hospitality, rather than describing a wider operating business. That distinction gives the activity its useful clarity. It is a code for a private training operation whose stated purpose is to deepen vocational skill and professional competence in hospitality.

The registration picture is broad on business scale. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar enterprises, so the record does not reserve it for a single size of operator. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. The national record therefore allows this activity to be wholly foreign-owned. The applicable source is identified as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021; beyond that source reference, the record does not add further national conditions.

Bali does not reverse that national openness. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently. This activity is not blocked by that rule. The record identifies the OSS risk at the Besar scale as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—and states that it is therefore not blocked by the moratorium. Its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: a concise indication that the relevant Bali position is openness in the higher-risk classification, not a PMA prohibition.

For a founder, the point is straightforward but worth holding precisely. This is a private hospitality training activity that may be registered at any of the listed scales, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In Bali, the permanent PMA moratorium remains part of the regulatory landscape, yet the record expressly places this activity outside its block because of the risk classification noted at the Besar scale. The result is an activity that is nationally open and, on the Bali record provided, not blocked for PMA registration by that moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium does not block this activity because the record places it in the higher-risk category at the Besar scale.
